questions: When nested elements share the same tag, how exactly should their values be merged? For example, if two sibling <item> elements have text 'a' and 'b', should the CSV row be 'item, a b' (space-separated), 'item, a,b' (comma), or something else?
Does 'merging their values' apply only to immediate siblings, or also to nested elements with the same tag at different depths (e.g., a parent <item> and its child <item>)?
Should the CSV include a header row? If so, what column names should be used?
How should XML attributes be handled? Should they be ignored, included as separate columns, or merged with element text?
What should happen if an element has no text content (e.g., <tag></tag> or <tag/>)? Should it be omitted, included with empty string, or something else?
Is the order of rows in the CSV important? Should it follow document order (depth-first), or some other ordering?
Should the CSV file be opened with a specific encoding (e.g., utf-8) or newline handling?
If the XML contains special characters (e.g., commas, quotes, newlines), should they be escaped in the CSV according to CSV standards?
